newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to cut vodka, ethanol imports from 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia to cut vodka, ethanol imports from 1997.

text.p: Russia on Sunday said it would bring in drastic import quotas for vodka and ethanol from January 1, 1997 in a move aimed at protecting domestic producers.
Itar-Tass news agency said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin signed an order introducing 1997 import quotas of 100 million litres of vodka and 10 million litres of ethanol.

Russian producers have complained that the cash-strapped national industry has badly suffered from a flow of cheap and low-quality foreign spirits, much of it imported tax-free from neighbouring states.
Experts have estimated the average annual import of vodka and ethanol at 1.27 billion litres. Official figures were not immediately available.

Sevodnya daily newspaper quoted the State Statistics Committee as saying that Russia imported $552 million worth of alcoholic drinks in the first half of 1996. This figure also includes grape wines and spirits other than vodka and ethanol.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment.
Tass said Russia would allow the import of 10 million litres of vodka from Ukraine and another 5 million litres from other former Soviet republics.
It added that Russia had still to negotiate with the European Community and the United States their share in the overall quotas.

Many experts and government officials have been involved in debates about whether introducing import quotas could help domestic alcohol producers or would only harm them by artificially easing competition at home.
Opponents of the limitations have said that the Russian alcohol market is far from saturated and that national producers could operate alongside importers.

The business daily newspaper Kommersant has quoted experts as saying that the national industry produced 1.21 billion litres of vodka and ethanol in 1995 with total market demand between 2.6 and 2.7 billion litres.
